title: Homes for All budget service expansions
subtitle: Seniors' care, airport staffing, housing maintenance, a rejected notice waiver, and a waste diversion report request
overview: The Strategic Planning and Budget Committee reviewed the 2024 budget under the Homes for All priority and recommended a series of staff service expansions. These cover the 4 Hours of Care expansion in Seniors' Services, land readiness and development staff, two airport positions, housing programs staff, Waterloo Region Housing facilities maintenance staff and design and construction project managers. All of these go to final budget day for Council's decision.

The committee also recommended that staff take no further action on the service-level and funding reduction options in the staff report. It defeated a motion to waive notice so a councillor's request for a report on filling the new land readiness roles from existing staff could be heard that day. That request will go through the normal notice process.

The committee recommended asking staff to report back on November 29 on a waste diversion strategy, with construction materials added. Staff will also return on November 22 with more information on homelessness funding and other items. Members noted the current tax levy position of 8.3 per cent.

decisions.item: 4 Hours of Care in Seniors' Services
decisions.detail: The committee recommended including the 4 Hours of Care service expansion in the 2024 operating budget {{vote:m2}}, which staff said is fully provincially funded.
The committee recommended including the Land Readiness and Development service expansion in the 2024 operating budget {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended funding an airport construction coordinator and an airport electrician in the 2024 operating budget {{vote:m5}}.
The committee recommended adding a Housing Programs Advisor, an Equity, Diversity and Inclusion advisor and 2 housing staff for Building Better Futures units {{vote:m6}}.
The committee recommended adding 6 facilities maintenance staff for Waterloo Region Housing and 3 facilities staff to replace contractor work {{vote:m7}}.
The committee recommended adding 3 project managers for capital project delivery in the 2024 operating budget {{vote:m8}}.
The committee recommended that no further action be taken on the service-level and funding reduction options in report COR-CFN-23-038 {{vote:m9}}.
The committee recommended directing staff to report back on November 29 on a waste diversion strategy {{vote:m10}}, with construction materials added by amendment {{vote:m11}}.

debate: On land readiness staffing, one councillor said they could not support more staff without information on whether existing planning and engineering roles could be reprioritised. Staff said the economic development team was at capacity and borrowing from other departments, and that Council would need to say what services to stop.

Other councillors opposed asking for another report. They said staff had already presented their best estimate and that further work would take time from other priorities. The procedural discussion centred on whether notice of a new motion could be waived, and the waiver was defeated {{vote:m3}}.

On the airport, councillors asked whether the electrician and construction coordinator roles were essential. Staff said airside electrical work is needed to meet federal standards and had been contracted out, and that facilities electricians lacked capacity. Another councillor raised aviation's climate impact, and staff pointed to a sustainability component in the airport master plan.

On the overall budget, councillors raised the tax impact and the share of the levy paying for services that the province should fund. One said further cuts may be needed. Others said earlier cuts were later reversed, and staff said the easy savings were already found.

On waste diversion, the mover described it as upstream and future-focused, asking only for information. One councillor raised concerns about landfill costs and a shrinking market for recycled materials, and opposed it.
